sections.section_title: Pathophysiology and Epidemiology of Behçet’s Disease
sections.description: Provides foundational knowledge on the immunopathogenesis, diagnostic criteria, demographic patterns and typical neurological manifestations pertinent to understanding the patient’s condition.
subtopics: Neutrophil hyperactivity and cytokine milieu (IL‑1β , IL‑6)
Typical CNS involvement – parenchymal lesions vs aseptic meningitis
Epidemiological trends – age distribution, ethnicity variability

sections.description: Outlines the patient’s symptom chronology, physical findings and laboratory clues that guided early suspicion toward both systemic Behçet’s disease and an endocrine disturbance.
subtopics: Chief complaints – fever, headache, hiccups, arthralgia
Mucocutaneous signs – oral aphthae, folliculitis-like rash, genital ulcer
Vital signs – tachycardia without hypotension indicating euvolemia
Initial laboratory findings – marked hyponatraemia with low serum osmolality
Early endocrine work-up consistent with SIADH (elevated ADH × urine osmolality)
